races.name: Dragon Symbol Standing At Whitsbury Manor British EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Whitsbury Manor Stud Supporting Inspire Foundation Handicap

runners_data.name: King Of Stars
runners_data.note: Returning after a 273-day absence for Michael Appleby, who has had zero wins from 23 runners over the past 14 days; hold-up style over 5f on Good ground suits the surface but the lengthy layoff and age-9 profile make it hard to trust him cold.|

runners_data.name: The Thames Boatman
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes has two wins from 44 runners in the past 14 days; this horse is a genuine hold-up type by nature, and with multiple other closers in the field it is likely to find itself squeezed into a midfield position that dilutes its finishing power, even though it did win over 5f on Good ground nine days ago.|

runners_data.name: Silver Wraith
runners_data.note: Emma Lavelle sends out a 4yo with a clean win over 6f on Firm and placed efforts on Good to Firm; the prominent style is ideally suited to tracking a single front-runner and deploying a one-move challenge, though its two most recent 5f runs have ended in seventh place, suggesting the step back to the minimum trip is a mild query.|

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Seamus Cronin (5lb claimer) takes the ride for Richard Hannon, whose stable is 9 from 46 in the past 14 days; a winner over 5f on both Soft and Good to Firm, this horse is a natural closer whose tendency to race at the rear means it will be held up in a field loaded with the same profile, making it harder to find clear daylight.|

runners_data.name: Fresh Fade
runners_data.note: Three-year-old running for Michael Attwater (0 wins from 6 in 14 days), with a form string of 045-60 that shows no recent encouragement; hold-up style and poor recent turf form on Good ground make it the least likely beneficiary of any race shape here.|

runners_data.name: Connie's Rose
runners_data.note: Grace Harris has 2 wins from 18 in the past 14 days; this 7yo front-runner wears a tongue-strap and hood combination and has placed twice at 5f on Good ground recently, giving her proven ability to sustain a lead at this trip — the lone pace-setter in a small field on a flat, fast track is her ideal scenario.|

races.paceDynamic: Connie's Rose is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and, with no genuine rival to press her for the lead, she should dictate from the off at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good to Firm ground over this sharp 5f at Salisbury. The hold-up contingent — King Of Stars, Fresh Fade, The Thames Boatman and Cayman Tai — is numerically dominant but that means the closers will be racing against each other for the same ground late, with no guaranteed bunching of pace to exploit. Silver Wraith is the one prominent-style runner who can sit just off Connie's Rose and is ideally placed to pounce if the front-runner ties up, without having to come from too far back. This race shape firmly favours front-to-prominent runners: an uncontested pace-setter in a small field on a flat, quick track creates a scenario where the lead is never surrendered cheaply, and hold-up horses face a wall of horses between them and the winner. The field contains more hold-up types than the rear of the map can naturally accommodate — The Thames Boatman and Cayman Tai are genuine closers who are likely to be shuffled into a midfield position they do not naturally seek, diluting their effectiveness.

scenarios.title: Connie's Rose Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Connie's Rose breaks cleanly and sets a controlled, uncontested pace, the race is run entirely to her strengths.
scenarios.body: If Connie's Rose breaks cleanly and sets a controlled, uncontested pace, the race is run entirely to her strengths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Wraith tracks Connie's Rose perfectly and times a challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Silver Wraith tracks Connie's Rose perfectly and times a challenge inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Connie's Rose goes too hard early and the pace collapses inside the final 2f, gifting the hold-up horses a run.
scenarios.body: If Connie's Rose goes too hard early and the pace collapses inside the final 2f, gifting the hold-up horses a run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically — pace collapses and the field fans wide — giving a lightly-regarded runner a clear passage.
scenarios.body: If the race falls apart tactically — pace collapses and the field fans wide — giving a lightly-regarded runner a clear passage.

watchPoints.text: Connie's Rose's early break is the race's hinge point — if Ray Dawson bounces her out of the stalls and she immediately goes unchallenged, the race shape is set and hold-up horses are immediately fighting a losing tactical battle.

The Thames Boatman and Cayman Tai are both natural hold-up horses but are likely to be racing closer than ideal given the field composition — watch whether either ends up tracking Connie's Rose involuntarily, which would improve their chance but is against their natural grain.

Silver Wraith's last two runs over 5f produced a seventh and a second over different distances; if the drop back to the minimum trip catches her out for pace early, she may find herself further back than intended and unable to deliver her challenge.

King Of Stars is returning from 273 days off — watch the market for any unusually strong support, as Michael Appleby's runners can be fit fresh but the trainer's recent form is poor and the horse is 9 years old.

Fresh Fade's weight of 134lbs is the lightest in the field for a 3yo, but her form figures of 045-60 on Good ground suggest she is struggling for her best at this stage of the season — notable only if she shows early pace that disrupts the race map.

races.name: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Havana Grey Standing At Whitsbury Manor Handicap

runners_data.name: Addison Grey
runners_data.note: Consistent course-and-distance performer with eight runs on similar going yielding two wins and five placed efforts — David Probert keeps the ride and the prominent, close-tracking style is perfectly suited to a race where Jel Pepper is expected to set a manageable tempo.|

runners_data.name: Another Abbot
runners_data.note: William Haggas's hold-up type arrives on a 33-day break with tongue tie fitted and a peak OR of 88, but the lack of genuine pace to close into makes this a difficult race shape for his natural style.|

runners_data.name: Jel Pepper
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front runner who should dictate unopposed on this fast surface, though a STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 tempers confidence — the form string of 71-466 suggests a horse that has not always delivered on that lead, and the step down from a recent win came on longer trips.|

runners_data.name: Sudden Flight
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's horse is a natural prominent racer who has finished second and third on similar ground at this distance, but the overcrowded early positions mean he is likely pushed back into a role his two-win OR-86 profile does not favour.|

runners_data.name: Egoli
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old arrives at a career-high OR of 90 with a form string that reads poorly on the surface but with two course-distance runs at this level providing experience — a prominent tracking style suits the expected race shape if Hector Crouch can get him travelling.|

runners_data.name: Fleetwater
runners_data.note: David Egan takes over on this J S Moore four-year-old who has placed at this distance on soft and standard, but the horse's front-running instincts are squeezed out by the pace map — competing effectively from an unnatural midfield berth will require a near-perfect run.|

runners_data.name: Queue Dos
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 76, Queue Dos carries the same J S Moore stable flag as Fleetwater and is another whose prominent racing style has been redistributed to midfield — a recent win came on standard going over 6f but the combination of inferior weight and out-of-role position makes this a tough ask.|

races.paceDynamic: Jel Pepper is the confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine rivals pressing for the lead on this going report confirming Good To Firm conditions throughout the card, should be able to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable gallop over the 6f at Salisbury. Addison Grey and Egoli are the natural prominent horses most likely to slot in directly behind, tracking what will be a controlled early pace rather than a scorching one. The field actually contains more front-running and prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate — Sudden Flight, Fleetwater, and Queue Dos are all natural prominent types who will find themselves unable to secure their preferred positions and will be shuffled into a midfield role they do not naturally suit. A sustainable, uncontested lead for Jel Pepper sets this up as a race where horses tracking close to the pace from positions two and three carry the clearest tactical advantage — prominent racers who can maintain contact without burning energy disputing the front will be best placed to pounce in the final furlong on this flat track.

scenarios.title: Jel Pepper Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Jel Pepper goes unchallenged to the front and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop that the field tracks without pressing.
scenarios.body: If Jel Pepper goes unchallenged to the front and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop that the field tracks without pressing.

scenarios.body: If Addison Grey or Egoli track Jel Pepper tightly and the pace proves just brisk enough to set them up for a strong final-furlong finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of Sudden Flight, Fleetwater, or Queue Dos manages to push forward from their mapped midfield position and reclaim a prominent pitch despite the crowded early exchanges.
scenarios.body: If one of Sudden Flight, Fleetwater, or Queue Dos manages to push forward from their mapped midfield position and reclaim a prominent pitch despite the crowded early exchanges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the front runners tie each other up and the race becomes a cavalry charge in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses or the front runners tie each other up and the race becomes a cavalry charge in the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Addison Grey has recorded two wins and five places from eight runs on similar going and is positioned directly behind an uncontested front runner — if Jel Pepper sets a comfortable tempo, Addison Grey is the horse most likely to inherit the lead at the furlong pole.

Sudden Flight, Fleetwater, and Queue Dos are all natural prominent horses who will contest the same positions in the early stages — watch for crowding or interference around the two-furlong marker if any of them attempt to push forward and reclaim ground.

Jel Pepper's STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 and a form string that includes three consecutive defeats invite caution — if the horse is not travelling as cleanly as expected at halfway, the pace scenario collapses and the entire race shape shifts.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this 6f slot throughout the day — ground has not changed and horses with a strong record on this surface, particularly Addison Grey and Sudden Flight, carry that advantage unchanged into the race.

Another Abbot is the only true hold-up runner and arrives from William Haggas with a tongue tie fitted — monitor the market for any stable confidence signal, as a significant move in the betting would suggest connections believe the pace scenario will suit him better than the map currently implies.

runners_data.name: Gone By
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's front-runner has won and placed twice from the front over 10-11f on Good and Soft, and steps up to 1m4f on Good to Firm where his uncontested lead looks a genuine asset — Hector Crouch can dictate every fraction in a three-runner field.

runners_data.name: Pearl River
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 3yo has won twice and been placed at 10f on Good and Soft going, but this represents a 4f step up in trip at 1m4f; Joe Leavy will track Gone By prominently, and her five recent runs have all been over 10f so the stamina question is real.

runners_data.name: Mythical Valentine
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly has shown progressive form at 11-12f on Good ground with a win and two placings in her last three, and the step to 1m4f is an obvious fit — Callum Hutchinson will sit just off the pace and she is the one most likely to be helped by the distance increase.

races.paceDynamic: Gone By is the sole confirmed front-runner in a three-horse field and will lead from the outset at Salisbury's 1m4f trip, with neither Pearl River nor Mythical Valentine carrying the inclination or form to challenge for the front. With just two prominent-style rivals tracking behind, Gone By faces zero pressure for the lead and can dictate a completely uncontested, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground. Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has already won and placed from the front over this sort of trip and going, meaning the pace is entirely in his hands — he can control fractions, conserve energy, and pick up off his own tempo. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner: a single pace-setter dictating an unchallenged rhythm on fast ground at a track where holding a lead into the straight is a genuine advantage rewards leaders and prominently-positioned horses far more than it does hold-up types, of which there are none in this field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Gone By dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and kicks off the home turn before rivals can close.
scenarios.body: If Gone By dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and kicks off the home turn before rivals can close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Gone By sets a slow early pace that bunches the field and Pearl River or Mythical Valentine produce superior finishing power.
scenarios.body: If Gone By sets a slow early pace that bunches the field and Pearl River or Mythical Valentine produce superior finishing power.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Step Up Suits Mythical Valentine
scenarios.trigger: If the step to 1m4f proves a significant advantage for Mythical Valentine, whose best form has come over 12f with further to come.
scenarios.body: If the step to 1m4f proves a significant advantage for Mythical Valentine, whose best form has come over 12f with further to come.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Chaos Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the race becomes a three-way sprint over the final two furlongs with no clear winner.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely and the race becomes a three-way sprint over the final two furlongs with no clear winner.

watchPoints.text: Gone By's ability to fully control the pace unchallenged in a three-runner field is the race's central dynamic — if he is not pressed, watch whether he quickens early enough off the home turn to make the race a procession.

Pearl River's trip stamina is unproven beyond 10f; if she weakens in the final furlong after tracking prominently, Mythical Valentine — who has raced over 12f — could emerge as the dangers closer to home.

The Good to Firm going (confirmed in the going report for this race) is faster than the Soft ground Pearl River has won on recently; watch whether the quicker surface stretches her stamina over the longer trip.

With only three runners, pace collapse is a real possibility — if Gone By sets an unusually slow tempo, the race effectively becomes a sprint over the final 2-3 furlongs and sectional speed rather than stamina will decide the outcome.

Mythical Valentine is dropping 11lbs below Pearl River in the weights (124lbs vs 133lbs) and has the most recent experience over this sort of trip; Hutchinson's positioning in the early stages will be the key tactical signal to watch at the start.

races.name: Molson Coors Handicap

runners_data.name: Hot And Cold
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's patient returning runners often come ready on debut back, but 224 days off is a substantial layoff for a 3yo filly — she is expected to lead and control the tempo, though her stamina for this trip and fitness level after such a gap are the key questions; rated going as OK, she steps up to 1m on good-to-firm.|

runners_data.name: Dark Sovereign
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's consistent 3yo has finished 2nd-4th on similar going (2/4 on good) without winning, and Hector Crouch's booking is solid; classed as unknown style, he is likely to race in midfield but his flat record against similar rivals makes him an each-way interest rather than a banker.|

runners_data.name: Lyra Lea
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner who sets up perfectly as a pace-stalker here — Rod Millman has had a runner in the last 14 days and Lewis Edmunds is an experienced claimer; she has placed twice on similar ground from nine qualifying runs and her two-place record on soft-skewing tracks may convert better on today's fast surface.|

runners_data.name: Legacy Rock
runners_data.note: In fine recent form with back-to-back wins at this trip and a strong strike-rate (2W3P from 8 runs on similar going), he is fundamentally a front-running type who is pushed into a midfield mapping here because the position has been claimed; the style mismatch is the primary risk, but raw ability on going that suits makes him competitive from wherever he settles.|

runners_data.name: Station Bar
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's hold-up specialist has winning form on firm ground (1/8f/FIR) and Charles Bishop gives this yard reliable handling; 35 days off is not a concern, but the likely controlled tempo is a genuine tactical problem for a horse that needs something to close into and has only one win from nine relevant-going runs.|

runners_data.name: John Harrison
runners_data.note: Alan King's 3yo has been off 178 days, which is a notable concern going into a competitive handicap, and his hold-up style leaves him reliant on a strong pace or a late injection — David Egan is a positive booking but there is only 1 placing from 4 similar-going runs and his form string includes some weak efforts.|

races.paceDynamic: Hot And Cold is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with just six runners and no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be able to control this from the front at Salisbury's 1m trip without being harassed or pressured into an unsustainable gallop. Lyra Lea is a natural prominent type who may push for a position close behind, while Legacy Rock — a genuine front-runner in normal circumstances — is redistributed into midfield because Hot And Cold is expected to claim that position and the field cannot accommodate multiple pace-setters at the front. Station Bar and John Harrison will settle in behind from their hold-up roles and rely on any fade from the leader late on, but on good-to-firm ground with an uncontested pace, those closers will need something to go wrong in front. The tactical verdict here favours a prominent or lead-tracking profile: with one horse likely to set a measured, unhurried gallop, those racing close to the pace in second or third will be best placed to pounce should the leader tire, while true hold-up horses face the classic problem of a steady pace giving them nothing to close into. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than can all secure their natural position, and Hot And Cold — with 224 days off and Sir Mark Prescott's patient preparation — is most likely to actually lead, with Lyra Lea best placed to grab the second spot.

scenarios.body: If Hot And Cold leads at a measured gallop and Lyra Lea or a tracking runner stays close enough to challenge turning in.

scenarios.body: If Hot And Cold's long absence (224 days) tells in the final furlong and the hold-up horses find a clear run.

scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Nothing Finishes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so conservative that the entire field is bunched turning in and the race becomes a sprint from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If the pace is so conservative that the entire field is bunched turning in and the race becomes a sprint from 2f out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Legacy Rock Forces Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Legacy Rock's connections push him forward despite redistribution, creating a contested early pace that scrambles the shape.
scenarios.body: If Legacy Rock's connections push him forward despite redistribution, creating a contested early pace that scrambles the shape.

watchPoints.text: Hot And Cold (224 days absent) — watch whether Sir Mark Prescott has her tuned up on debut back, as her fitness level will determine whether the tempo she sets is truly sustainable or collapses in the final furlong.

Legacy Rock's gate and early position — if connections press him forward against type to try to reclaim his natural lead role, a contested early pace scrambles this entire shape and dramatically improves the hold-up horses' prospects.

Lyra Lea's position leaving the stalls — if she misses the break or is outpaced to the prominent spot by Dark Sovereign, she loses the ideal tracking position that this pace map assigns her and her chance diminishes sharply.

Station Bar and John Harrison — both true hold-up horses on a day when the going report confirms good-to-firm conditions across the card; watch whether either is fitted with any gear changes or positioned more aggressively than expected, as that would signal a tactical switch worth noting.
